overall: The AG did not decide whether the Council or redistricting committee violated the Open Meeting Law at the fall 2022 events. It found any violations were cured by later properly noticed deliberative meetings, ordered no further action, and treated one complaint as time-barred.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged a quorum of councilors and redistricting committee members deliberated on redistricting at several events outside posted meetings in fall 2022.
allegations.key_passage: Although we need not decide whether the Council or Committee committed a violation of the Open Meeting Law at this stage, the complaints are not without merit

allegations.summary: Council argued any violation from the fall 2022 events was cured by later properly noticed meetings, including the May 2023 map vote.
allegations.key_passage: We, too, are satisfied that the several properly noticed meetings that the Council held in late October 2022, as well as further meetings in May 2023 culminating in the vote on May 24, 2023, satisfactorily cured any violations of the Open Meeting Law as alleged in the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged members serially discussed redistricting in City Hall offices; the Council denied this.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the complaints in the instant matter present other contested factual issues as well.

allegations.summary: One complaint, filed in April 2023 about September 2022 conduct, was reviewed for timeliness under the 30-day filing requirement.
allegations.key_passage: A complaint alleging a violation of the Open Meeting Law must be filed with the public body within 30 days of the alleged violation.
